sections.label: Debt restructuring framework amendments
sections.summary: MinLaw considered ILRC and debt restructuring committee recommendations, prompting amendments in three categories including transparency, regulatory burden and debt restructuring.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) has also considered the recommendations of the Insolvency Law Review Committee (ILRC) and the Committee to Strengthen Singapore as an International Centre for Debt Restructuring to enhance Singapore's debt restructuring framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These reviews have prompted the current amendments which fall into three categories.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, amendments to improve the transparency of ownership and control of companies in line with certain international norms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Second, amendments to reduce the regulatory burden and improve the ease of doing business and, third, amendments to enhance our debt restructuring framework.

sections.label: Amendments and transitional period
sections.summary: The amendments aim to maintain Singapore's reputation as a trusted financial hub, to be effected by 31 March 2017, with a 60-day transitional period for registers of controllers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These amendments will boost Singapore's ongoing efforts to maintain our strong reputation as a trusted and clean financial hub.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We intend to effect these amendments by 31 March 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To help companies prepare to comply with these new requirements, existing companies will have a transitional period of 60 days from the commencement of the law to maintain the registers of controllers.

sections.label: AGM and annual return deadlines
sections.summary: Listed companies must hold AGMs and file annual returns within four and five months after financial year end; non-listed companies within six and seven months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill will require listed companies to hold AGMs and file annual returns within four months and five months after their financial year end respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Non-listed companies must hold AGMs and file annual returns within six months and seven months after their financial year end respectively.

sections.label: Adapted Chapter 11 features
sections.summary: Adapted Chapter 11 features include an automatic moratorium of up to 30 days, worldwide effect, and extension to related entities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Features of Chapter 11 that will be adapted include: providing an automatic moratorium on filing an application, for a period of up to 30 days; allowing the Court to give the moratorium worldwide effect; and extending the moratorium to related entities relevant to the restructuring.

sections.label: Super-priority for rescue financing
sections.summary: The Court will be empowered to order that rescue financing be given super-priority.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To facilitate rescue financing, the Court will be empowered to order that rescue financing be given super-priority.

sections.label: Judicial management order threshold
sections.summary: Clause 25(a) allows a judicial management order when a company is likely to become unable to pay its debts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 25(a) will allow the Court to make a judicial management order when a company "is likely to become unable to pay its debts", as opposed the current "will be unable to pay its debts".

sections.label: UNCITRAL Model Law adoption
sections.summary: Clauses 41 and 50 adopt the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency (1997), a framework governing recognition and assistance of foreign insolvency proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clauses 41 and 50 adopt the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency (1997), which is a well-understood and internationally respected framework that governs the recognition and assistance of foreign insolvency proceedings.

sections.label: Winding up applications 2016
sections.summary: In the first half of 2016, Singapore had 118 winding up applications, with 85 companies put into liquidation, high versus the previous 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2016, there were 118 winding up applications in Singapore, out of which 85 companies were then put into liquidation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is high when compared to the previous 10 years.

sections.label: Offshore marine industry workers
sections.summary: The offshore and marine industry, probably the hardest hit sector in the recent downturn, employs some 88,000 workers in that sector alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The offshore and marine industry, probably the hardest hit sector in the recent downturn, has some 88,000 workers employed in that sector alone.

sections.label: Automatic 30-day moratorium welcomed
sections.summary: In that context, the automatic 30-day moratorium upon an application being made in Court is very much welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In that context, the automatic 30-day moratorium upon an application being made in Court is very much welcomed.

sections.label: New cram-down provisions
sections.summary: The new cram-down provisions allow the company or a creditor to apply to Court for scheme approval despite objection by a class of creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The new cram-down provisions, however, meet this criticism nicely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: They allow the company or one of its creditors to apply to Court for approval of the scheme, notwithstanding that it is objected to by a class of creditors.

sections.label: Earlier judicial management amendments
sections.summary: The amendments allow a company to be placed into judicial management as long as it is likely to become unable to pay its debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: To allow the judicial management regime to be more effective, it ought to be possible to implement it at an earlier stage to give distressed companies a real prospect of success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That is why I welcome the amendments which allow for a company to be placed into judicial management as long as it "is likely to become" unable to pay its debts.

sections.label: Rescue financing priority and security
sections.summary: The amendments encourage financial institutions to give rescue financing by letting Courts grant priority or security for that debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The amendments incentivise and encourage financial institutions to provide rescue financing, by giving the Courts the power to grant priority or security in relation to the debt created under the rescue financing arrangements.

sections.label: UNCITRAL Model Law recognition applications
sections.summary: The UNCITRAL Model Law supplements insolvency laws, letting a foreign insolvency practitioner apply to the Singapore Court for recognition of foreign proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, this was an issue which came up in a recent High Court decision in the Pacific Andes case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is where the UNCITRAL Model Law comes in to supplement our insolvency laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Under this framework, a foreign insolvency practitioner can apply to the Singapore Court for recognition of insolvency or restructuring proceedings in another country.

sections.label: Countries adopting the Model Law
sections.summary: Countries adopting the Model Law include the US, UK, Australia, Japan and Korea, which are leading restructuring jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Other countries, like Singapore, which have adopted the Model Law, include the US, the UK, Australia, Japan and Korea, amongst others, and these are the leading jurisdictions in which restructurings take place.

sections.label: Singapore restructuring hub and Amendment Bill
sections.summary: A Global Restructuring Review report said London and New York face competition from Singapore, and the Bill is part of that effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In a recent publication by Global Restructuring Review on 1 March 2017 just last week, it was reported that this "traditional hegemony of London and New York" is facing competition from Singapore, following the concerted push to make ourselves a leading restructuring hub for the Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The amendments which this Bill seeks to introduce are an integral part of that effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Amendment Bill came up for First Reading only last Tuesday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, after eight days of the Budget and Committee of Supply debates, this Bill is up for Second Reading and debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A large part of this Bill is the result of the recommendation by ILRC back in October 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope all Members have time to digest the Bill in such a short time, as we ought to.

sections.label: Unpaid debts to shipping businesses
sections.summary: Many debts owed to shipping and other businesses worldwide remain unpaid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In reality, I understand that many debts owed to many shipping and other businesses worldwide are still unpaid.

sections.label: Unsecured creditor recovery in Hanjin case
sections.summary: As in the Hanjin case, unsecured creditors often end up with limited or no recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, like in the Hanjin case, unsecured creditors will quite often end up with limited or no recovery.

sections.label: Bill adopts UNCITRAL Model Law
sections.summary: The Bill adopts the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill adopts the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency.

sections.label: Supporting ratifying Model Law in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker supports ratifying and applying the Model Law in Singapore, noting relatively few countries have ratified it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Though relatively few countries have ratified the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency, for the reasons I have given above, I am of the view that we should support ratifying and applying the Model Law in Singapore.

sections.label: Article 25 amendment and ring-fencing
sections.summary: Article 25 was amended from "shall cooperate" to "may cooperate"; the speaker asks why and about abolishing the ring-fencing mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Article 25 was amended by substituting "shall cooperate" to the maximum extent possible with foreign courts or foreign representatives to "may cooperate" instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify why this amendment was made?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Also, in relation to cross-border insolvency is the abolishment of the ring-fencing mechanism, which has been criticised by practitioners local and abroad as contrary to internationally-accepted standards of a fair and equitable cross-border insolvency regime.

sections.label: Foreign companies transferring incorporation to Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendment allowing foreign companies to transfer their registration of incorporation to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I support the amendment to allow foreign companies to transfer their registration of incorporation to Singapore.

sections.label: First financial year 18-month limit
sections.summary: Proposed section 198(2) provides the first financial year must be no longer than 18 months unless ACRA approves on the company's application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The proposed section 198(2) provides that the first financial year must be no longer than 18 months, unless ACRA approves on the application of the company.

sections.label: Companies Act amendments ground-breaking
sections.summary: The Companies Act amendments incorporate elements from US Chapter 11 and adopt the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Companies Act is ground-breaking in at least two ways: the incorporation of elements from US Chapter 11 into our corporate insolvency regime which has English roots; and two, the adoption of the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency.

sections.label: Judicial management and scheme enhancements
sections.summary: The amendments make judicial management orders easier to apply for and add enhanced moratorium, rescue financing and cram-down provisions for schemes of arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the amendments, it is now easier for companies to apply for a judicial management order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There will also be enhanced moratorium, rescue financing, cram-down and other enhancement provisions for the schemes of arrangements.

sections.label: Shareholders' cram-down proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests introducing some form of shareholders' cram-down to further improve the cram-down provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What I think we could do to create a further improvement to the cram-down provisions would be to introduce some form of shareholders' cram-down.

sections.label: Companies (Amendment) Bill changes
sections.summary: The Bill implements changes in the Companies Act, including enhanced moratoriums against creditor action, rescue finance and cram-down provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Companies (Amendment) Bill implements various changes in the Companies Act, such as providing for enhanced moratoriums against creditor action in judicial management, rescue finance and cram-down provisions.

sections.label: Register of controllers and nominee directors
sections.summary: The new Part XIA requires companies to keep a register of controllers and nominee directors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The new Part XIA of the Companies (Amendment) Bill requires companies to keep a register of controllers and nominee directors.

sections.label: Registers of controllers requirement
sections.summary: The Bill requires non-listed locally incorporated companies and foreign companies to maintain registers of controllers and identify registrable controllers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, the Bill proposes to amend the Companies Act to require non-listed locally incorporated companies and foreign companies to maintain registers of controllers and to take reasonable steps to find out and identify registrable controllers of the company.

sections.label: Imputing officers' state of mind
sections.summary: Proposed section 386AD imputes the state of mind of a corporation's officers, employees or agents to the corporation for Part XIA offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, the proposed section 386AD of the Bill imputes the state of mind of the corporation's officers, employees or agents to the corporation itself in respect of offences under the proposed new Part XIA.

sections.label: Lower standard limited to Part XIA
sections.summary: The question asks why the lower standard in section 386AD of the Bill applies only to offences under the new Part XIA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In these circumstances, why limit the application of the lower standard in section 386AD of the Bill only to offences under the new Part XI A?

sections.label: Ministry says levers adequate
sections.summary: The Ministry replied that current legislative and regulatory levers against errant companies are adequate and no specific provision is needed now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Ministry's reply was that the current legislative and regulatory levers that we have to take action against errant companies are adequate and there is no need at this point for a specific provision to penalise a company for failing to prevent a crime from taking place.

sections.label: Section 386AD and corporate states of mind
sections.summary: The question asks whether section 386AD signals a shift in attributing states of mind to corporations for other serious economic crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Legal persons, including foreign companies registered in Singapore, are vulnerable to criminal misuse." Given the FATF's report stating that companies in Singapore are vulnerable to criminal misuse, does the introduction of section 386AD signal a shift in the standard of attributing states of mind to corporations in respect of other serious economic crimes?

sections.label: Private institutions access to registers
sections.summary: The passage proposes considering whether wider access to registers of controllers should be allowed to certain specified categories of persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, there is value in allowing certain prescribed categories of private institutions, such as financial institutions, access to the register, as this would facilitate these institutions' conduct of due diligence on their customers or in respect of the financial transactions that they may facilitate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I propose that we consider whether wider access to these registers of controllers is beneficial and should be allowed to certain specified categories of persons.

sections.label: Shareholder cram down paradigm shift
sections.summary: The passage states that introducing shareholder cram down requires a fundamental paradigm shift because neither requirement exists in the current framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The current cram-down provisions ensure that the scheme distributes a company's property to its creditors in a fair and equitable manner and are not concerned with adjustments to shareholder interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In order to justify cramming down shareholders' rights, shareholder meetings must be called and the company should be shown to be insolvent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Neither requirement exists in the current framework, so a fundamental paradigm shift to the regime is required to introduce shareholder cram down.

sections.label: Re-domiciled company treated as Singapore-registered
sections.summary: Under the new regime, a re-domiciled company is treated as a Singapore-registered company upon issuance of the Notice of Transfer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under the new regime, a re-domiciled company will be treated as a Singapore-registered company upon issuance of the Notice of Transfer.

sections.label: Minimum retention period five years
sections.summary: The Bill sets a minimum retention period of five years, after considering the five-year period set by FATF and GF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Bill sets out the minimum retention period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have set it at five years after considering the five-year period set by FATF and GF.

sections.label: EU Fourth Anti-Money Laundering Directive
sections.summary: In June 2015 the European Union issued the Fourth Anti-Money Laundering Directive requiring member states to maintain central or public registers of beneficial owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In June 2015, the European Union issued the Fourth Anti-Money Laundering Directive to require member states to maintain central or public registers of beneficial owners.

sections.label: Access restricted to Registrar and agencies
sections.summary: As this will be a new register, access is restricted only to the Registrar and public agencies for administering and enforcing their respective laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As this will be a new register, we decided to take a more conservative approach by restricting access to the register only to the Registrar and public agencies for the purpose of administering and enforcing their respective laws.

sections.label: Pacific Andes worldwide moratoriums jurisdiction
sections.summary: In the Pacific Andes Resources Development case heard in September last year, the High Court held it did not have jurisdiction to grant worldwide moratoriums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan may recall a Pacific Andes Resources Development case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That was heard in September of last year and our High Court held that we did not have the jurisdiction to grant the worldwide moratoriums.

sections.label: Substantive activity for tax purposes
sections.summary: From the Singapore perspective, there must be substantive activity for tax purposes, and Singapore does not wish to be a centre for tax purposes without underlying substantive activity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In so far as tax and corporate re-domiciliation are concerned, it is very important to establish or reiterate that, from the Singapore perspective, we are a jurisdiction where there must be substantive activity for tax purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We certainly do not wish to be a centre where you just come here purely for tax purposes without any underlying substantive activity.

sections.label: MAS bespoke resolution regime
sections.summary: This was done with input from MAS because financial institutions have a bespoke resolution regime administered by MAS to restructure these entities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This was done with input from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the reason is that, for financial institutions, there is a bespoke resolution regime which is administered by MAS to restructure these entities.

sections.label: Minister designating financial institutions
sections.summary: The amendments let the Minister designate additional financial institutions, a specialist track under MAS purview, to be emplaced soon after the Bill passes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What the amendments do is they will allow the Minister to designate some additional financial institutions but, primarily, it is because it is a specialist track and this is something which really best comes under the purview of MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that the sooner this is emplaced, the better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As soon as possible after this Bill is passed.
